questions.learningObjective: express concentration in parts per million
questions.stem: Sample 0301: A sample contains 35.0 mg of analyte in 2.97 kg of solution. What is the concentration in parts per million?

options.misconception: multiplies the mass terms instead of taking their ratio
inverts the ratio of analyte mass to sample mass
adds a factor of one thousand already contained in the units

questions.explanation: One part per million is one milligram of analyte per kilogram of sample, so the concentration is simply the milligram mass divided by the kilogram mass. Multiplying by an extra factor or inverting the ratio misuses the definition of the unit.
questions.hint: Parts per million is milligrams per kilogram.

questions.learningObjective: compute molarity from mass, molar mass, and volume
questions.stem: Measurement 0302: 38.09 g of a compound with molar mass 74.0 g/mol is dissolved to make 0.85 L of solution. Determine the molarity?

options.misconception: adds a superfluous unit-conversion factor

multiplies by molar mass instead of dividing

questions.explanation: Molarity is moles of solute per liter of solution. Converting grams to moles requires dividing by molar mass, and dividing by the volume in liters then gives the concentration. Multiplying by the volume or by molar mass gives the wrong quantity.
questions.hint: Convert to moles, then divide by liters.
